segments.text: [softly] Lie down and arrange the body for twenty minutes of unhurried rest. Imagine a warm cabin while snow gathers quietly outside.
Feel the whole body beneath its coverings. Nothing needs to be held up. The roof, walls, and earth are doing the work.
Right thumb... first finger... second... third... fourth... palm... back of hand... wrist. Snow softens every edge.
Right lower arm... elbow... upper arm... shoulder... armpit... right ribs... waist... hip.
Right thigh... knee... shin... calf... ankle... heel... sole... top of foot... big toe through little toe.
Left thumb... first finger... second... third... fourth... palm... back of hand... wrist.
Left lower arm... elbow... upper arm... shoulder... armpit... left ribs... waist... hip.
Left thigh... knee... shin... calf... ankle... heel... sole... top of foot... big toe through little toe.
Backs of both legs... buttocks... tailbone... lower back... middle back... upper back... shoulder blades... back of neck.
Lower belly... navel... upper belly... ribs... heart area... collarbones... throat. The cabin stove glows without needing attention.
Chin... jaw muscles... lower lip... upper lip... corners of mouth... teeth... gums... tongue lying loose in the floor of the mouth.
Inner cheeks... outer cheeks... nose... nostrils... bridge of nose... skin beneath the eyes.
Right eye... left eye... both eyelids... muscles around the eyes... eyebrows... the soft space between them.
Forehead smoothing... temples... ears... back of skull... top of head... entire scalp. Let the face finish its last conversation.
Feel the entire right side... entire left side... both sides together... back body... front body... complete body.
[reassuringly] You may feel heavy, light, restless, or nearly asleep. The snow does not require a particular kind of quiet.
Rest as the whole cabin, not one room at a time. Breath moves softly through the warm interior.
Let several long moments pass with the complete body known at once.
Begin hearing the real room. Feel temperature, coverings, floor, and the shape of the body returning.
[softly] Move fingers and toes, roll the head gently, and stretch if desired. Open your eyes as snowlight reaches the windows.
